lines.text: the grammar is never just math — it is always also a claim about what counts as growth
Seven presets, one turtle — the grammar is the artist
lines.note: the editor rewrites every rule but never the turtle — F has no meaning any production can supply — and by the depth where the drawing finally reads as a plant, the rule has disappeared inside its own output.

note_src.quote: A different interpreter could read the same string and produce a different geometry.

lines.text: One rule, one angle, one axiom — a tree grows
The string is the structure — the tree is just one way to read it
Context sensitivity is how real trees grow — the environment is part of the grammar
lines.note: the grammar has no symbol for the wall: the tree must grow a branch into the obstacle before it can prune it, so the shape that records the corridor is paid for in branches attempted and clipped.

note_src.quote: You can only clip a branch that the grammar prescribed.

lines.text: Watching a tree grow generation by generation teaches more than seeing the final form
Randomness in the parameters, not the rules, is what makes grammar look like nature
Context-Free Grammars visualizer — animated parse trees showing Chomsky hierarchy (regular → context-free → context-sensitive → …
lines.note: the rule does not fill a given space, it constitutes the grid it visits — so every point exactly once holds only in a limit with no final generation, and the floor can exhibit only the resolution where you stopped.

lines.text: Change the angle from 25° to 90° and the tree becomes a city
lines.note: the grammar writes streets and nothing else: the blocks, the lots, everything a city is lived in is the space the rules failed to reach — the inhabited part is a remainder no production can name.

note_src.quote: The lots are the regions the streets failed to reach.

lines.text: Two rules and a turtle — the dungeon writes itself
Competition emerges when grammars share resources — ecology is grammar plus scarcity
A coral is not one tree — it is many grammars growing from the same rock
lines.note: scarcity appears in no grammar: light, soil, the coral's shared rock are state the rules never mention, so a losing tree is not a wrong grammar but a silenced one — shaded out by whoever reached the canopy first.

note_src.quote: The grammar still exists — the rules have not been erased — but they have been functionally silenced.

lines.text: A tree is eight numbers — change them and you are doing what evolution does
lines.note: the sculptor has eight genes and no fitness function — selection needs a value neither the grammar nor the forest can supply — so the learner's taste is the unstated term, and the world then judges it by light alone.

note_src.quote: The values come from somewhere the code cannot see.

pearls.edge: a production rule reads only its own string, so the vine cannot answer without something outside both grammars measuring the learner's branch angle and handing it over — the dialogue depends on a translator neither side wrote.

edge_src.quote: the vine sprouts new laterals whose branch angles mirror the incoming structure

lines.text: the excavation record was never impersonal. The general intellect has a face here
Gödel as furniture — the limit is not a bug to fix but the shape of the thing
every sufficiently powerful formal system contains true statements it cannot prove
lines.note: that the weaver and the logician want the same thing is a claim about both systems and provable inside neither, so the room carries it as an axis between cloth and proof — an argument only a walking body collects.

note_src.quote: The room is arranged so the weave and the proof have to look at each other.
